items.title: IAM least privilege
items.passage: Grant the actions needed for a task on appropriate resources and conditions. Broad Allow permissions merit review; a Deny wildcard does not grant permissions. Some AWS actions do not support resource-level permissions, so Resource * alone is not proof of administrator access.

items.title: IAM principals and conditions
items.passage: A wildcard Principal represents all principals. Conditions can restrict a statement; inspect their semantics before calling access unrestricted. Effective access also depends on identity policies, boundaries and other controls absent from a plan. Scope role trust to intended principals.

items.title: Security group rule sources
items.passage: Rules define protocol, ports and IPv4 or IPv6 sources. Allow database traffic from application security groups; allow web traffic through the load balancer. World-open administrative and data ports merit restriction. Reachability additionally depends on routes, network ACLs and service configuration.

items.title: RDS public accessibility
items.passage: Public accessibility assigns a public IP and changes external DNS resolution. Actual external access still requires suitable security group ingress, internet gateway and subnet networking. Publicly_accessible=true alone does not prove that arbitrary internet clients can connect.

items.title: RDS encryption and migration
items.passage: RDS encryption protects underlying storage, logs, backups and snapshots. Encryption cannot simply be enabled on an existing unencrypted DB instance; use an encrypted snapshot copy and restore workflow. Plan migration, downtime and key access before changing encryption.

items.title: RDS backup retention
items.passage: A DB instance retention of zero disables automated backups. Changing between zero and nonzero retention causes an outage. Alternate backup coverage and restore readiness need human confirmation.

items.title: S3 Block Public Access
items.passage: S3 Block Public Access overrides public policies and ACLs. S3 uses the most restrictive combination of applicable organization, account, bucket and access-point controls. Disabling a bucket setting increases possible exposure but does not by itself prove objects are publicly readable.

items.title: S3 default encryption
items.passage: Since January 5, 2023, new S3 uploads automatically receive SSE-S3 encryption. Absence of an explicit Terraform encryption resource does not establish unencrypted storage. Existing objects, customer-managed key requirements and access to keys need separate verification.

items.title: TerraGate production deletion policy
items.passage: Project policy: production deletion or replacement of a stateful resource is critical and requires a reviewed exception, verified restore point, owner signoff and rollback plan. The plan proves the destructive action, not whether backups or approvals exist.

items.title: TerraGate production recovery policy
items.passage: Project default policy requires production DB deletion protection and at least seven days of automated backup retention. Use the selected policy pack values if different. A planned reduction below policy requires review; missing or unknown controls require verification, not a claim of confirmed failure.

items.title: EBS encryption and snapshot migration
items.passage: EBS encryption uses KMS keys to protect volumes and snapshots. Existing unencrypted volumes require a snapshot and new encrypted volume; encryption and key changes are not simple in-place edits. Verify key access and migration plans. A size-only update retaining encryption is not a loss of encryption.
